newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to sell Svyazinvest to Russians, foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Russia to sell Svyazinvest to Russians, foreigners.

text.p: Russia intends to sell lots in state telecom holding company Svyazinvest to both Russian and foreign investors, starting in early 1997, Communications Minister Vladimir Bulgak said on Thursday.
"The doors for investment here are open to everyone who wants to, both abroad and in Russia," he told a news conference.

Bulgak denied a report in the Financial Times that the sale of shares in OAO Investitsionnaya Kompaniya Svyazi (Svyazinvest) would now be managed by the Most and Alfa banking groups, and that London-based investment bank N.M. Rothschild had been dropped as a consultant to the sale as a result.

"I want to say categorically that this is not true. We will attract to this process not only Russian banks, but also other financial structures and leading telecommunications companies, which may form a small consortium," he said.
On Tuesday the State Property Committee, Russia's privatisation ministry, said it was dropping Rothschild as consultant to the sale.
But Bulgak said the Russian authorities had been happy with Rothschild's work, and would like to work with it again on a subsequent sale of shares.
"We consider it advisable to attract Rothschild for a further placement of shares both on the domestic market and abroad," he said.

The authorities have not conducted negotiations with any Russian banks on managing the sale, he said. Some Russian banks had expressed interest in buying shares in Svyazinvest but only on a non-discriminatory basis, he said.
The attempt last year to sell a 25 percent stake in Svyazinvest to a strategic partner included only foreign companies.
But there had been speculation that the decision to drop Rothschild would result in a sale structured to allow a small group of banks close to the government to buy the shares.
Bulgak said he hoped the property committee would make it possible for Russian banks to take part in the sale, but the decree on the sale has not yet been approved.

Bulgak said Russia had decided to sell Svyazinvest shares to portfolio investors rather than a strategic investor because it was not possible to find a single partner who could make the necessary investments, which he put at $1.5 billion.

Italy's state telecoms holding company Stet SpA won the original tender for 25 percent of Svyazinvest last year with a bid of 2.93 trillion roubles for the shares and a promise to invest 3.5 trillion roubles -- about $1.4 billion at exchange rates at the end of last year.

The size of the investment needed was underlined by an announcement from Swedish telecoms equipment group L.M. Ericsson that it had signed a framework agreement with Svyazinvest to deliver $145 million of switching equipment and services in 1997-98. The equipment will be delivered to regional operators as determined by Svyazinvest.
Bulgak said the value of a 25 percent stake in Svyazinvest ranged from $2 billion to $4 billion according to different estimates.
But deputy Communications Minister Valentin Boldin said selling the stake in several lots over 1-1/2 years could raise the price.

As part of the changed strategy for selling Svyazinvest, the government plans to transfer its 38 percent stake, equal to 51 percent of the voting shares, in Rostelekom RTKM.RTS 0#RTKM.RUO to Svyazinvest, which holds large government stakes in 85 regional telecoms companies.
But Bulgak said there were no plans to merge the two companies.
